newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Reforms, stability seen boosting Philippine growth.
newsitem.headline: Reforms, stability seen boosting Philippine growth.

text.p: The Philippines' strong economic growth in the first half of 1996 surpassed expectations and showed that economic reforms and political stability were beginning to bear fruit, a senior government official said on Saturday.

Raphael Lotilla, acting director general of the National Economic Development Authority, told a news conference that growth was fuelled by a strong export performance and investment inflows, especially in the booming construction sector.

Gross national product growth of 7.06 percent in the first half of 1996 against 5.6 percent in the same 1995 period was also boosted by a rise in remittances from Filipinos working overseas, Lotilla said.
These remittances reached 19.7 billion pesos in the first half.
"This is a hefty 76.5 percent increase over last year's first (half) level and is due to higher perosnal and property income inflows," Lotilla said.

Some four million Filipinos, out of a total population of 68 million, work abroad. Recent Central Bank figures showed that around 70 percent of the remittances came from Filipinos living in North America.
The growth figures were well above analysts' expectations. A Reuter poll of Manila brokerages produced an average first-half GNP forecast of just 6.4 percent.
"The first (half) performance of the economy shows that, indeed, the past economic reforms in an environment of enhanced peace and political stability are beginning to bear fruit," Lotilla said.
He added that a second quarter recovery in the agriculture sector had also contributed to growth, along with "declining inflation and interest rates couple with the stable peso".
